newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL noon rubber up, prices erratic on ringgit fear.
newsitem.headline: KL noon rubber up, prices erratic on ringgit fear.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber market was higher at midday, but traders said prices were erratic due to worries over the immediate direction of the ringgit.

Shortcovering demand for the SMR10 and SMR20 was emerging after weeks of bearish sentiment but buyers and sellers could not agree on prices due to uncertainties over whether the ringgit would strengthen or weaken, said traders.
"The (SMR)20, sellers are asking at around 240 (cents a kg) but the buyers are looking 234," said a trader.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 buyer for August at 230 cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Monday's close. The board priced SMR20 buyer for August a cent higher at 233.50.
Traders quoted the SMR 20 at 240 cents, SMR CV at 296, SMR L at 280, SMR5 at 247, SMR10 at 242 and drum latex at 193.
The INRO's five-day average price also strengthened at 182.27 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 14, compared to 182.07 on July 11. The daily indicator rose to 183.92 from 182.63 previously.
Malaysian-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
